objection: Our price was about 20% above FreightIQ's quote.
stakeholder_concern: The VP of Operations feared implementation would disrupt peak-season shipping.
pricing_discussion: Buyer asked for a 20% discount. We offered 8% for a two-year term, and they countered with FreightIQ's number.
approach: Led with discounts and never built an ROI case or a phased rollout plan.
outcome_reason: FreightIQ undercut on price and, with no quantified ROI, procurement treated the purchase as a commodity decision.

objection: No evidence of HIPAA compliance was available during the security review.
stakeholder_concern: The CISO was worried about exposure of patient health information.
pricing_discussion: No discount was requested; the fixed quote was accepted without negotiation.
approach: Shared SOC 2 Type II report and a HIPAA BAA early, ran a joint security workshop with the CISO, then a 45-day pilot.
outcome_reason: The security workshop and pilot resolved the CISO's concerns, so price never became the deciding issue.

objection: The proposal felt too complex and feature-heavy for a credit union of their size.
stakeholder_concern: Branch managers were afraid of the training burden on busy staff.
pricing_discussion: Buyer asked for a per-seat discount; we moved to tiered seat pricing instead of cutting the rate.
approach: Right-sized the scope to the Team Plan and included onboarding and training at no extra charge.
outcome_reason: A simplified scope and free onboarding matched their budget and removed the training worry.

objection: Their team said they could build the same reporting themselves.
stakeholder_concern: The IT lead did not want to onboard another vendor.
pricing_discussion: No pricing discussion took place; the deal never reached a quote.
approach: Ran a technical feature demo for the analyst team with no business case and no executive contact.
outcome_reason: There was no executive sponsor, and the do-it-yourself option was seen as free, so the deal quietly faded.

objection: Budget was frozen until the next fiscal year.
stakeholder_concern: The CFO required payback in under 12 months.
pricing_discussion: We proposed a three-year contract with a 30% year-one ramp discount instead of a flat discount.
approach: Built an ROI model jointly with the CFO's team and tied the ramped pricing to quarterly milestones.
outcome_reason: Ramped pricing fit within the current budget and the ROI model showed a nine-month payback.

objection: FreightIQ's quote was 15% cheaper than ours.
stakeholder_concern: The Operations Director wanted a fast go-live with minimal disruption.
pricing_discussion: We held list price and instead presented a total-cost comparison that included FreightIQ's paid integrations.
approach: Delivered a total-cost-of-ownership comparison and arranged a reference call with a similar logistics customer.
outcome_reason: The cost comparison showed FreightIQ was more expensive once integration fees were counted, and the reference call built trust.

objection: The security questionnaire was long and the buyer required EU data residency.
stakeholder_concern: The Head of Compliance feared audit findings from an unproven vendor.
pricing_discussion: We conceded a 10% discount early, before the security issues were resolved.
approach: Sent generic questionnaire answers late and never engaged our own security lead with their compliance team.
outcome_reason: Slow, generic security responses and no EU data residency option; the early discount did not repair trust.

objection: Procurement demanded a 25% discount and a three-vendor comparison.
stakeholder_concern: Clinical operations leaders worried about system downtime during rollout.
pricing_discussion: We refused 25% and traded a 10% discount for a three-year commitment with annual prepayment.
approach: Engaged the CFO as executive sponsor, negotiated on value, and offered a phased rollout with an uptime guarantee.
outcome_reason: Trading discount for term and prepayment, plus executive sponsorship and an uptime guarantee, overcame procurement pressure.

objection: As a nonprofit their budget was too small for our standard price.
stakeholder_concern: The Dean wanted easy adoption by faculty who resist new tools.
pricing_discussion: Buyer asked for an education discount; we gave 15% in exchange for annual billing.
approach: Offered the education discount and ran a faculty-champion training program.
outcome_reason: The education discount fit the budget and the champion program addressed faculty adoption.

objection: The buyer said the add-on duplicated their existing BI tool.
stakeholder_concern: The analytics manager championing us was considering leaving the company.
pricing_discussion: We quoted list price and no negotiation occurred.
approach: Relied on a single champion and never built relationships with other stakeholders or an executive sponsor.
outcome_reason: The champion left the company mid-deal and nobody else had been engaged, so DataLens won by default.

objection: Their legal team pushed back on the liability cap and automatic renewal terms.
stakeholder_concern: The General Counsel feared unlimited liability exposure and being locked into renewals.
pricing_discussion: There was no price pushback; the discussion focused on contract terms.
approach: Brought our own legal counsel in early, agreed a mutual liability cap, and removed auto-renewal.
outcome_reason: Early legal alignment resolved contract objections before they could delay signature.

stakeholder_concern: The store operations manager wanted a simple mobile experience for store staff.
pricing_discussion: We cut the price by 22% to get close to Stackwise without changing the scope.
approach: Discounted deeply with no scope change and did not differentiate on mobile experience or value.
outcome_reason: Won by matching most of the price gap, but margin was thin and the renewal is at risk of another price fight.

objection: The buyer wanted proof of value before committing to a contract.
stakeholder_concern: The Managing Partner doubted advisors would actually adopt the tool.
pricing_discussion: Buyer asked for a free pilot; we proposed a paid 60-day pilot credited against the contract.
approach: Ran a paid pilot with written success criteria agreed up front and weekly adoption reviews.
outcome_reason: The paid pilot with defined success metrics demonstrated adoption and converted straight into the contract.

objection: New vendor onboarding through procurement was expected to take six months.
stakeholder_concern: Plant managers worried about integration with their legacy manufacturing execution system.
pricing_discussion: The quote expired while waiting; the buyer then asked for an extension plus a 12% discount.
approach: Waited passively for procurement, set no deadline, and had no executive engagement.
outcome_reason: There was no compelling event, the quote lapsed, and momentum was lost during the long procurement queue.

objection: The buyer was concerned the tool would not integrate with their electronic health record system.
stakeholder_concern: The Clinical Director had been burned by a failed software rollout the previous year.
pricing_discussion: Standard pricing was accepted with no discount request.
approach: Built an integration proof of concept against their EHR sandbox and arranged a reference call with another healthcare customer.
outcome_reason: The proof of concept de-risked integration and the reference eased fears from the previous failed rollout.

objection: FreightIQ bundled security features at no extra cost.
stakeholder_concern: The CISO needed compliance reports to show the company's own customers.
pricing_discussion: At the last minute we offered an 18% bundle discount, without having shown the value of the pack.
approach: Offered a late bundle discount and did not demonstrate customer-facing compliance reporting.
outcome_reason: The late discount came without proven value, so the buyer took FreightIQ's free bundled security.
